review.summary: Attempt 4 closes the three low findings from attempt 3. compare_reference now scans an inline replacement of a parameter, body or response $ref before emitting. Existing security schemes fail closed on unknown keys. Added operations have their servers and security scanned, and changed servers are scanned too. CLASSIFIER_VERSION is 4 and the ledger matches it. In the recorded checks for source a220e2a…, every exit code is 0: airs_drift --check, 46 drift tests including the new reference/servers/security/schemes test, --require-through-phase 25, and an unchanged SDK diff. One minor gap from attempt 3 is still open: a non-dict schema that becomes a dict at a property-name pointer is not scanned. There are also smaller unscanned shapes in security changes on existing operations and in security-scheme flows. All are low. Total 45/50.

findings.description: compare_schema's non-dict branch emits type_changed at the caller's pointer. When that pointer ends in a property name (for example a boolean schema `true` becoming a dict with discriminator or x-*), line 438 does not scan the new side, because the last pointer part is not in SCHEMA_SUBTREES and is not an int. The attempt-3 finding named this case explicitly, and it is still unresolved.
findings.required_fix: In the non-dict branch, call self.scan_schema(new, parts) when new is a dict before emitting. Add a test that changes a property from `true` to `{discriminator: ...}` and expects 'no receipt written'.

findings.description: When an existing operation's security changes, it is emitted as security_changed without scan_security. A malformed requirement (for example non-list scopes) is classified instead of failing closed, while the same shape on an added operation fails.
findings.required_fix: Call self.scan_security(new['security'], parts + ['security']) before emitting security_changed. Add one test.

findings.description: SECURITY_SCHEME_KNOWN checks only top-level scheme keys. An x-* key or an unknown key inside 'flows' (or inside a flow object) on an added or changed scheme is classified as security_scheme_changed or treated as additive.
findings.required_fix: Validate flow names (implicit, password, clientCredentials, authorizationCode) and flow keys (authorizationUrl, tokenUrl, refreshUrl, scopes) in both scan_component and compare_security_scheme.

The 'response-ref-to-inline' test replaces the existing GET /v1/channels 400 response (a $ref to BadRequest in the pinned network-broker YAML, lines 190 and 252) with inline content, so it exercises the compare_reference scan path.

The behavior in plan lines 254-303 (offline check and compare, refresh as the only networked path, unknown changes fail with no receipt) matches the implementation and the test classes.
limitations: Read-only review. I did not run tests or tools myself; all execution evidence comes from the recorded checks file.
I read about 600 lines of the 3278-line checks file and used grep for the rest (exit codes, test counts, airs_drift entries).

I did not re-audit red_team_management.py, check_phase.py, test_management_phases.py or the vendor 0.86.0 bytes beyond their passing recorded checks. Earlier attempts accepted them, and this attempt's changes are in airs_drift.py and its tests.
I found the remaining gaps by reading the code and did not reproduce them with a run.
I did not examine remote CI or a live pan.dev refresh.
